target.title: fix(discord): keep thread title truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

- AI-assisted with Codex; I inspected the changed production path and can explain the change.
- Discord thread-title prompt/context truncation now preserves UTF-16 boundaries for long source/channel fields.
- The prompt construction is exposed as `buildThreadTitleCompletionUserMessage` so the formatting path can be validated directly without requiring a live completion provider.
- Intentionally out of scope: unrelated truncation sites, response-read bounding, config changes, and behavior outside this specific thread-title formatting boundary.

## Linked context

- No linked issue.
- Related to the existing OpenClaw UTF-16-safe truncation hardening pattern.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior addressed:** Discord thread-title prompt/context truncation should not leave a dangling surrogate when long message, channel name, or channel description text is cut at the configured limits.
- **Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout on Node v22.22.0; PR head `f062226e814bd229e3f20ab5b454c100ea009fc6`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-title.generate.test.ts`
  - Standalone `node --import tsx --input-type=module` invocation of `buildThreadTitleCompletionUserMessage` from the current PR head.
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-title.generate.test.ts
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts
RUN  v4.1.9 /tmp/openclaw-utf16-prs/discord-thread-title
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  9 passed (9)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 23.47s
```

Standalone formatting-path transcript from the same head:

```text
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module  # imports buildThreadTitleCompletionUserMessage
node=v22.22.0
head=f062226e814bd229e3f20ab5b454c100ea009fc6
path=buildThreadTitleCompletionUserMessage
contentLength=1089
messagePrefixSafe=true
channelPrefixSafe=true
descriptionPrefixSafe=true
contentContainsEmoji=false
contentHasLoneSurrogate=false
```

- **Observed result after fix:** the thread-title prompt formatting path emits safe truncation markers for message, channel name, and channel description; the boundary emoji is not split into the output and no lone surrogate remains.
- **What was not tested:** full Discord deployment and live third-party completion provider delivery were not run; this proof is scoped to the touched thread-title prompt formatting path.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** no private credentials or live completion provider were required; the standalone proof directly executes the production prompt formatter used by `generateThreadTitle`.
- **Before evidence (optional but encouraged):** raw JavaScript string slicing can cut between a high and low surrogate at these boundaries, producing malformed text in prompt context.

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-title.generate.test.ts`
- Standalone runtime transcript shown above.
- Added focused direct formatter coverage for message, channel name, and channel description UTF-16 boundary cases.
- No known local failures from this change.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes. Malformed truncated prompt/context text is now avoided while preserving existing caps and truncation markers.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

No.

What is the highest-risk area?

Discord thread-title prompt/context formatting.

How is that risk mitigated?

The patch is limited to the existing truncation boundaries, uses the existing UTF-16 helper, and now has focused regression coverage plus standalone direct formatter proof.

## Current review state

What is the next action?

ClawSweeper re-review and maintainer review.

What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?

Nothing is waiting on the author after this update; waiting on CI/ClawSweeper/maintainer review.

Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed?

Addressed ClawSweeper's needs-proof feedback with a direct Node/tsx transcript from the current PR head that invokes the changed thread-title formatting path and shows `contentHasLoneSurrogate=false`.
